name: Seated Calf Raise
cues: Sit with the pad snug over your lower thighs, just above the knees
Rest your forefoot on the platform edge, heels free
Let your heels drop fully before each rep
Press up through your big toe and hold the top briefly

qa.note: Family review 2026-10-01 rated minor. review: A front close-up shows the knee pad on the lower thighs just above the knees, with the knees at 84-90 deg. The heel travels well below and above the roller. The hero view hides the pad behind the plate horns and forearms, but the calves and grips read. | skeptic: Mechanics are right: knees 84-90, heel from 71 mm below the ball (ph 0.625) to 70 above (ph 0), thighs under the lever pad (-8 mm), the forefoot on the bar (-3.5 mm), and the thigh angle follows the knee rise (hip 90-103). Things for the owner: the handles stand about 20 cm above the pad on the lever, so the hands grip at lower-chest height with the elbows flexed 135-140 deg (a curl-like arm, see review-figure/figure-602-side.png). That is an unusual prop design, since seated calf handles usually sit at the pad. In the hero (-130/0.24) the pad over the lower thighs, which is cue 1, is mostly hidden behind the forearm and plate and only a sliver shows. | skeptic: The knee/thigh pad is not visible in the hero (figure-602.png) or the side sheet (side/figure-602-side.png). The plate and horns cover it, so the viewer never sees the load contact on the thighs. The stretch is also shallow: at t=0.5 to 0.75 in the side sheet the sole looks almost horizontal, and in the foot close-up the heel is only about 2 cm below the roller top, although the angle plot says DF 24. Hands are closed on the horns and the calves read.
